summary: Iteration 4 testing: multi-user teams, personalized greeting, dashboard tabs, and global quick-create menu. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_iteration4.py — 5/5 tests pass covering GET /api/team (owner listed with is_you=true, role='owner'), unauth 401, invite validation (400 on missing fields), full invite flow (temp_password returned, member appears in list, invited user can login and sees the same seeded customers = shared org data confirmed, duplicate invite rejected 400, non-owner cannot DELETE 403, owner DELETE 200 and member removed from list), and owner-self-remove blocked (400). Frontend Playwright: login as owner OK; dashboard shows personalized greeting ('Good morning/afternoon/evening, Aniruddh'); dashboard-tabs with dash-tab-overview/finance/operations all present and switch. Header quick-create-button opens menu; all six quick-create-{customer,invoice,expense,product,task,lead} items navigate to /<module>?new=1 and auto-open crud-modal (or invoice-modal for invoices). Settings tab-team renders team-members list with owner badge; invite-name/invite-email/invite-role/invite-submit produces invite-result with generated email/temp-password and increments member count; remove-member-<id> opens ConfirmDialog and confirm-accept removes the member (verified members count returns to baseline). No console errors observed. Cleaned up 1 leftover TEST invite user created during the first UI test attempt.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py /team/invite returns temp_password in cleartext response body — acceptable for demo/MVP but production should email the invite link with a signed one-time reset token instead of exposing the password to the inviter.
server.py /team/invite lower-cases email but does not validate format (no EmailStr Pydantic model). A malformed email would still create a user record; consider Pydantic validation.

server.py /team GET returns all org members with 'role' but no distinction between 'admin' and 'member' is enforced anywhere else in the codebase — role is stored but not gated in any endpoint. Currently only owner-vs-non-owner matters (for DELETE). If admin is meant to have elevated privileges, no endpoints check for it yet.

TeamTab.js: after successful invite, credentials are shown in plain text on-screen and remain visible until page reload — consider auto-dismissing after copy or after 30s, and offering a 'regenerate' action.

TeamTab.js remove flow assumes optimistic backend response; if DELETE fails partway, load() is still called silently in success — the current error branch does show toast but does not re-open the ConfirmDialog. Minor UX only.

Header.js quick-create dropdown uses fixed navigation to /<module>?new=1 — for pages that live behind ProtectedRoute this works, but there's no feedback if the user lacks permission (all users are effectively owner today so N/A right now).

success_rate.frontend: 100% of iter4 critical flows (greeting, dashboard tabs, quick-create all 6 modules, team invite + shared-data proof, remove-member + confirm)

seed_data_creation: None permanent. During UI testing, temporarily invited 'test_ui_*@example.com' users and cleaned them up via the remove flow at end of test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter4 feature-set (team invite/list/remove, quick-create dropdown, personalized greeting, dashboard tabs) is fully green. When running the Playwright UI test for team, always use a unique email (uuid) — duplicate invite returns 400 'already a member'. Regression testids in header are 'currency-selector' (not currency-toggle) and 'theme-toggle-button' (not theme-toggle). Confirm dialog testid is 'confirm-accept'. Global search testid is 'global-search-input'. Backend seed reliably provides owner + 1 member (Jamie Lee) = baseline member count 2 in the Acme Global Ventures workspace.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found in iteration 4.
